heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P handles Bambu PETG HF exceptionally well right out of the box, reaching printing speeds up to 250 mm/s supported by an effective volumetric flow rate of 21 mm³/s. Because PETG HF is non-abrasive and performs reliably in an open-frame printer, no enclosure or nozzle upgrades are required.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 21 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent underextrusion at high feedrates.
Enable Wipe While Retracting with a 2 mm wipe distance to minimize fine PETG stringing and nozzle buildup.
Configure Nozzle Temperature to 245°C for all layers and Bed Temperature to 70°C to maximize inter-layer adhesion without sagging.
Set First Layer Speed to 40 mm/s and First Layer Infill to 50 mm/s to ensure consistent bed adhesion without ripping delicate lines.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine hair buildup on nozzle
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG HF is highly hygroscopic and absorbs ambient moisture quickly, causing steam micro-explosions and nozzle ooze.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated dryer at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing, and increase retraction distance to 0.8 mm.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: PETG tearing chunks out of the build plate during part removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Direct bonding of PETG to clean smooth or textured PEI can exceed the mechanical strength of the PEI coating.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of liquid glue or glue stick as an interfacial release agent, and let the bed cool down below 35°C before removing parts.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Matte finish and weak layer bonding on high-speed outer perimeters
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Printing outer walls beyond the thermal melting capacity of the hotend at high acceleration, causing poor plasticization.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Limit outer wall speed to 150-180 mm/s or raise nozzle temperature to 255°C within the allowable 230°C-260°C range.

faq.question: Do I need to enclose my Bambu P1P to print Bambu PETG HF?
faq.answer: No, Bambu PETG HF does not require an enclosed chamber. The open-frame design of the P1P works well because PETG benefits from moderate cooling and lacks the extreme thermal contraction tendencies of ABS or PC.

faq.question: Can I use the stock stainless steel nozzle on the P1P for PETG HF?
faq.answer: Yes, PETG HF is completely non-abrasive and does not contain carbon or glass fibers, so the standard stock stainless steel nozzle will not experience premature wear.

faq.question: Why is glue stick recommended if I am using a Textured PEI Plate?
faq.answer: On PEI surfaces, PETG forms an extremely aggressive chemical bond. A thin layer of glue acts as a sacrificial release agent rather than an adhesive, preventing the plastic from peeling away the PEI coating when removing the print.

faq.question: What is the recommended drying procedure for Bambu PETG HF?
faq.answer: Dry the spool at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours in an active filament dryer or oven. PETG absorbs moisture rapidly, which results in oozing, stringing, and reduced mechanical strength if left exposed to ambient air.
